cohort: The study cohort consisted of 183 infants who had bloodstream infection or meningitis reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and in the literature between 1961 and 2018.
finding: Invasive Cronobacter infection case counts significantly increased globally from 2004-2018, with higher proportions occurring among full-term and nonhospitalized US infants during this period, and PIF contamination was identified in 30% of investigations.
